title: Nested Routes
description: Learn how to create nested route structures for complex layouts.

data.text: **Nested routes** let you build hierarchical URL structures where a parent layout wraps child pages. This is the standard way to create dashboards, settings panels, and any UI with persistent sidebars or headers.
Place child `<Route>` elements inside a parent `<Route>`. React Router matches the parent first, renders its element, then renders the matching child inside it.

data.title: Nested Routes
data.code:
<Routes>
  <Route path="/" element={<Layout />}>
    <Route index element={<Home />} />
    <Route path="about" element={<About />} />
    <Route path="dashboard" element={<Dashboard />}>
      <Route index element={<DashboardHome />} />
      <Route path="stats" element={<Stats />} />
      <Route path="settings" element={<Settings />} />
    </Route>
  </Route>
</Routes>

data.text: `<Outlet />` is a placeholder inside a parent route's element where the matched child route renders.

data.title: Outlet

data.text: An **index route** renders when the parent path matches exactly. It acts as the default child route.

data.title: Index Route
data.code:
<Route path="/dashboard" element={<DashboardLayout />}>
  <Route index element={<DashboardHome />} />
  <Route path="analytics" element={<Analytics />} />
</Route>

// URL /dashboard renders DashboardHome
// URL /dashboard/analytics renders Analytics

data.text: A parent route without a `path` acts as a layout wrapper. It wraps its children without adding anything to the URL.

data.title: Layout Route
data.content: Wrapping routes without changing the URL

data.title: Outlet Naming
data.text: You can have multiple outlets with named outlets, but most apps use a single unnamed Outlet in the main layout.

terms.definition: A child route defined inside a parent route's element.
A placeholder in a parent route where the matched child renders.
The default child route rendered when the parent path matches exactly.

data.title: Exercise: Build a Dashboard Layout
data.description: Create a dashboard with a sidebar and nested pages.
steps: Create a DashboardLayout with a sidebar using Links.
Add nested routes for Home, Analytics, and Settings.
Use an index route for the default dashboard page.
Add an Outlet in the main content area.
data.expectedOutcome: A dashboard layout where navigation switches content without reloading.

items.question: Can I have nested layouts inside nested layouts?
items.answer: Yes. Nest as many layout routes as needed. Each level can have its own Outlet.

items.question: Why is my child route not rendering?
items.answer: Check that the parent route has an <Outlet /> and that the child path does not start with a slash unless it is absolute.

items.question: Do layout routes re-render when the child changes?
items.answer: Yes, by default. Wrap expensive layout parts in React.memo if needed.

items.question: What is the difference between path='' and no path on a layout?
items.answer: No path means the layout wraps children without contributing to the URL. path='' matches an empty segment and can be used for more precise control.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Nested routes create hierarchical URL structures.
Outlet renders the child route inside the parent layout.
Index routes act as the default child.
Layout routes wrap children without adding to the URL.
data.takeaway: Nested routes are the foundation of organized, multi-section SPAs. Next, you will learn dynamic route parameters.
